race_context: Confirmed: the township names match the Metropolitan School District of Warren County, which state election results list as 'Msd Of Warren County' for the Liberty & Pine, Pike & Jordan and Steuben & Kent seats {enr_2022}. The district is based in Williamsport and runs Pine Village Elementary, Warren Central Elementary, Williamsport Elementary and Seeger Memorial Junior-Senior High School in West Lebanon {msdwc_home}{wiki_msdwc}. Federal data list 1,332 students in 2024-25 {nces_msdwc}.

Superintendent: the district's posted administrative contracts show a superintendent contract running through June 30, 2028 at $126,000 a year but do not give a name {msdwc_contracts}. Wikipedia lists Ralph Shrader as superintendent; this guide did not find a current district page confirming it {wiki_msdwc}.

The district website lists five board members: Dr. Gary Greenwood (president, member since July 1998), Dan Duchemin (vice president, since August 2015), Dr. Brooke Max (secretary, since January 2019), Shawn Allison (since December 2021) and Sharon Grady (since January 2013) {msdwc_board}. Each seat is tied to a group of townships; Duchemin (Adams & Warren Twps) and Grady (Washington Twp) were last elected in 2024 {enr_2020}{enr_2024}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: three seats, one member each, matching the state list's 'vote for 1' {in_list}{enr_2018}{enr_2022}. Liberty & Pine Twps: incumbent Brooke Max is running against Mark DeGolyer. Pike & Jordan Twps: incumbent Gary D. Greenwood is running against Caleb Austin Winger. Steuben & Kent Twps: incumbent Shawn Allison is not on the 2026 list, so the seat is open between Kaitlin (Pence) Nigh and Timothy Fowler {msdwc_board}{enr_2022}{in_list}.

Party labels: five of the six candidates are listed as Republicans; Greenwood is listed as Nonpartisan {in_list}. In 2018 and 2022 all three of these seats were won by single, unopposed candidates on nonpartisan ballots {enr_2018}{enr_2022}.

Building project and possible petition: on Sept. 9, 2026 the board made a preliminary determination to issue bonds and enter lease agreements for renovations and improvements to facilities throughout the district, plus buses, equipment and technology, with an estimated principal of $65 million, a maximum annual lease rental of $5 million over up to 26 years, and estimated interest of $43,952,816 {msdwc_pd_notice}. The notice estimates the debt service tax rate would rise from $0.4818 to about $0.6930 from 2030, a net increase of $0.2112 {msdwc_pd_notice}. Under state law, if a valid petition is filed within 30 days of the notice's first publication, the project must go to voters in a local public question {msdwc_pd_notice}. The two required hearings were on the Aug. 10 and Sept. 9 agendas, and the board held a July work-session discussion with Ice Miller, Baker Tilly and Lancer Associates {msdwc_ag_20260810}{msdwc_ag_20260909}{msdwc_ag_20260715}.

Budget and staffing: the board's 2026 agendas included a bond refunding discussion in February, a staffing and budget review in June, a review of staffing and projected enrollment in August, and a hearing on the 2027 budget, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan on Sept. 9, with adoption set for Oct. 7 {msdwc_ag_20260211}{msdwc_ag_20260608}{msdwc_ag_20260810}{msdwc_ag_20260909}{msdwc_ag_20261007}. The Oct. 7 agenda also sought authorization to apply for additional appropriations for the Education Fund and possibly the Operations Fund {msdwc_ag_20261007}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects the district or on any operating referendum.

Records and forums: the district posts agendas and keeps meeting videos online for 90 days; older agendas and minutes are available on request {msdwc_board}{msdwc_ag_20261007}. This guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire, candidate website or news coverage of the candidates' views.
